search_tip: Cannot find a setting? Use the BIOS search (the footer of the screen shows the key, often F3, F7 or F9) and type the setting name.
order_note: Do the settings in this order: CSM off, then Above 4G Decoding, then Resizable BAR if you want it. Virtualization and IOMMU are independent.

vtx.label: Intel virtualization (VT-x)
vtx.why: Lets the CPU run virtual machines.

svm.label: AMD virtualization (SVM)
svm.why: Lets the CPU run virtual machines.

vtd.label: Intel VT-d
vtd.why: Lets the host hand a PCI card to one VM safely (the IOMMU).

amd_iommu.label: AMD IOMMU
amd_iommu.why: Lets the host hand a PCI card to one VM safely.

above4g.label: Above 4G Decoding
above4g.why: Lets the GPU's large memory window sit above 4 GB.

csm.label: CSM (legacy boot support)
csm.why: Must be off so the machine boots in pure UEFI mode.

primary_display.label: Primary display
primary_display.why: The motherboard's own graphics should show the boot screen, not the card you pass through.

rebar.label: Resizable BAR (optional)
rebar.why: Optional. If the VM will not start, turn it off.

virtualization.names: Intel Virtualization Technology, VT-x, VMX, SVM Mode, AMD-V, Secure Virtual Machine
virtualization.where: Usually under Advanced > CPU Configuration, Tweaker > Advanced CPU Settings, Settings > Advanced > CPU Features, or Security > Virtualization.

iommu.names: VT-d, Intel VT for Directed I/O, AMD IOMMU, IOMMU Support, AMD-Vi
iommu.where: Usually under Advanced > Chipset, North Bridge, System Agent (SA) Configuration, AMD CBS > NBIO Common Options, Miscellaneous (Gigabyte) or Processor Options (HPE).

above4g.names: Above 4G Decoding, Above 4GB MMIO, Memory Mapped I/O above 4GB, PCI 64-bit Resource Handling above 4G, Above 4G memory / Crypto Currency mining (MSI)
above4g.where: Usually under Advanced > PCI Subsystem Settings, PCIe/PCI/PnP Configuration, North Bridge or IO Ports (Gigabyte).

csm.names: CSM Support, Launch CSM, Legacy Support, Boot mode UEFI/Legacy, Legacy Option ROMs

primary_display.names: Primary Display, Initial Display Output, Initial Graphics Adapter, Primary Graphics Adapter, VGA Priority, Primary Video Device, Select Active Video
primary_display.where: Set it to IGD, IGFX, Onboard or iGPU. Servers keep the BMC graphics as the console and need no change.

rebar.names: Re-Size BAR Support, Resizable BAR, Smart Access Memory, Clever Access Memory
rebar.where: Appears only after Above 4G Decoding is on and CSM is off.

intel-nuc.name: Intel NUC
intel-nuc.mode: F10 opens the boot menu. Newer NUCs (13 and later) are made by ASUS and use the ASUS layout.

vtx.path: Security > Security Features > Intel Virtualization Technology
vtx.source: https://www.intel.com/content/dam/support/us/en/documents/intel-nuc/NUC-AptioV-BIOS-Glossary.pdf (Intel NUC Aptio V BIOS Glossary rev 2.0, p.30): Aptio V BIOS Page Security > Security Features

vtd.path: Security > Security Features > Intel VT for Directed I/O (VT-d)
vtd.source: https://www.intel.com/content/dam/support/us/en/documents/intel-nuc/NUC-AptioV-BIOS-Glossary.pdf p.30: Aptio V BIOS Page Security > Security Features (grayed out and forced on while Intel TXT is enabled)

above4g.path: Usually not offered. NUC 12/13 Extreme: Advanced > Devices > PCI > Above 4G Decoding
above4g.source: Not verified: the Aptio V glossary has no Above 4G item. Previous wording kept from memory.

csm.path: Boot > Boot Priority > UEFI Boot (enabled) and Legacy Boot (disabled)
csm.value: UEFI Boot on, Legacy Boot off
csm.source: https://www.intel.com/content/dam/support/us/en/documents/intel-nuc/NUC-AptioV-BIOS-Glossary.pdf Boot > Boot Priority: UEFI Boot and Legacy Boot checkboxes

mini-pc.name: Minisforum / Beelink and other mini PCs
mini-pc.mode: F7 opens the boot menu on many models. Mini PCs often hide advanced menus.

vtx.path: Advanced > CPU Configuration > Intel Virtualization Technology
vtx.source: Not verified: Minisforum and Beelink publish no BIOS menu documentation. Forum posts suggest Advanced > CPU Configuration > SVM Mode and Advanced > AMD CBS > NBIO Common Options > IOMMU on AMD models, but forums are not accepted sources.
